title: Add backup primitive for Private upgrades: control-plane DB + config state snapshot w/ verify + retention
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need a first-class backup primitive in the redwood-private-installer upgrade flow. This will be invoked as a required gate before applying any upgrade steps that can mutate state.

Scope
- Snapshot control-plane DB (Postgres) used by Redwood Private control plane.
- Backup config/state required to restore a functional Private deployment after a failed upgrade or operator-initiated rollback.
- Backup verification step that provides strong signal that the snapshot is usable (not just "command succeeded").
- Retention policy + cleanup logic that is safe by default and configurable.
- Testing plan for restore drill (automated where possible, documented runbook for manual).

Non-goals
- General-purpose cluster backup (full etcd or full PV snapshot for all customer workloads).
- Re-architecting customer storage/backups beyond what’s required for upgrade safety.

Primary users
- SRE/PS/operators running upgrades on Redwood Private in VPC and on-prem/air-gapped environments.

Why this matters
We have repeated failure modes where an upgrade gets part-way through (schema migration / chart apply) and leaves the deployment in a degraded state. Having a deterministic, verified snapshot before upgrade is a hard requirement for safe rollback and for Support to triage quickly.
acceptance_criteria:
Functional
- Installer provides a consistent "backup" step as part of the upgrade orchestration (and callable standalone) that:
  - snapshots the control-plane DB
  - archives the installer-known config state (rendered values + selected Kubernetes objects + installer metadata)
  - writes a backup manifest (what was captured, versions, correlation id, timestamp, hashes)
  - verifies the snapshot/backup before proceeding to upgrade

Verification
- Verification must fail closed (upgrade cannot continue if backup verification fails) unless explicitly overridden with a flag that is clearly labeled dangerous.
- Verification must be fast enough for typical maintenance windows, with clear progress output.

Retention
- Default retention: keep N most recent successful backups (proposal: 3) and/or max age (proposal: 14d), configurable.
- Cleanup must not delete backups created within the current in-progress upgrade run.

UX / Supportability
- Backup step emits structured logs and is tied to the upgrade correlation id.
- Installer prints where the backup lives and how to restore.

Docs / Runbooks
- Update runbook(s) to include backup/restore drill and expected RPO/RTO.

Testing
- Add at least one integration-style test path that exercises backup -> verify -> simulated failure -> restore -> health check.
- Provide a documented manual restore drill for on-prem/air-gapped where CI cannot execute full flows.
implementation_notes:
Design choices
- DB snapshot strategy:
  - VPC: use pg_dump to a writable, operator-specified location (recommended: S3-compatible object store). Rationale: avoids coupling to cloud-specific snapshot APIs and works across AWS/GCP/Azure. (We can add provider-native snapshots later.)
  - On-prem/air-gapped: pg_dump to local filesystem path with guidance to move the archive to external storage if required by customer policy.

- Config/state backup contents (minimum viable for rollback):
  - installer state file / metadata (including previous known-good version where present)
  - rendered Helm values for redwood-control-plane, gateway, runtime
  - Kubernetes objects needed to rehydrate installer-managed resources (selected namespaces, configmaps, secrets references; do not include secret values unless explicitly allowed)
  - versions: chart versions + control plane version (if available via version endpoint)

- Verification approach:
  - DB: after pg_dump, run pg_restore --list and a lightweight pg_restore --schema-only to a disposable temp DB (where feasible) OR run pg_dump --format=custom and validate archive integrity (exit code + list of objects) and ensure dump size > threshold.
  - Config/state: verify tarball integrity, compute and store sha256, ensure required files exist, and validate manifest schema.

- Retention:
  - Backups are written under a deterministic directory prefix: backups/<deployment-id>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ>-<correlation-id>/
  - Cleanup runs at start of backup step (after acquiring an installer lock) and only deletes backups that are:
    - marked successful
    - older than retention
    - not referenced by current in-progress upgrade record

- Safety / secrets:
  - Do not export secret values by default.
  - Manifest may reference secret names and namespaces, but must redact data fields.
  - Any credentials used for object storage must come from customer-provided environment variables / k8s secrets and must not be logged.

Owner interfaces
- Installer command surface (proposed):
  - redwood-private-installer upgrade run ... (invokes backup step automatically)
  - redwood-private-installer backup create --output <path|s3://...> [--retention-count N] [--retention-days D]
  - redwood-private-installer backup verify --backup <id|path>

Open questions (resolved in comments)
- Whether we require PV snapshots for control-plane DB in Kubernetes deployments. Current decision: not required for v1; rely on logical dump (pg_dump) and document limitations (RTO might be higher for large DBs).
testing_plan:
Automated (CI/integration harness)
1) Happy path: backup create -> verify -> proceed gate returns success.
2) Negative: corrupt the dump artifact (truncate file) -> verify fails -> upgrade run blocks.
3) Restore drill simulation: create backup -> apply a known breaking change to schema (or simulate failed migration) -> restore backup to temp DB -> control plane comes back healthy.

Manual (runbook)
- VPC staging environment: run backup create to S3, verify, then run restore and validate:
  - control plane API /healthz
  - version endpoint returns expected previous version
  - key workflows (login, model registry listing) succeed
- On-prem/air-gapped staging: run backup create to local path, copy tarball to a second node (optional), restore and validate same health checks.

Acceptance signals
- Restore completes within target maintenance window for staging-sized DB (initial target: <= 20 minutes end-to-end; document that customer DB size will vary).
- No secrets are present in the backup tarball by default (spot-check + automated grep for known keys).
risk_notes:
Risks
- Large DBs could make pg_dump slow; may exceed some customer maintenance windows. Mitigation: document expectations, allow compression level tuning, and consider incremental/provider-native snapshots as follow-up.
- Verification that relies on creating a disposable DB may not be possible in locked-down environments. Mitigation: support both "strong" verify (restore schema-only to temp DB) and "light" verify (archive integrity + object list + size thresholds), defaulting based on capabilities.
- Storage/IAM issues (VPC) are common failure modes. Mitigation: precheck for write permissions and bucket reachability before running pg_dump to remote target; emit clear remediation.

Operational constraints
- Must fail closed when backup/verification fails (no partial upgrades).
- Must produce logs suitable for diagnostics bundles (support escalation).

comments: 2025-01-16 (Devon Price): Drafted installer-level backup interface. Proposing logical DB dumps (pg_dump) as v1 for cross-environment support. Will coordinate with Security on what config/state is allowed to be archived (no secret values by default).
2025-01-20 (Ethan Park): +1 on pg_dump for v1. Please include control plane version + migration watermark in backup manifest so rollback checks can enforce forward-only migrations policy.

2025-01-22 (Marcus Lin): Reminder: ensure backup tarball does not include k8s Secret data unless explicitly opted-in. Also ensure object-store credentials never hit logs. Add redaction tests if feasible.

2025-01-27 (Sean Gallagher): For verification, prefer at least a pg_restore --list and a checksum + size sanity check. Temp DB restore is ideal but might be blocked in some customer environments; provide fallback verify mode with clear labeling.

2025-02-03 (Devon Price): Implemented backup create + verify and wired into upgrade run (PR #427). Added manifest (json) + sha256 for artifacts. Default retention: keep last 3 successful backups, prune older than 14d. Waiting on final review from Release Eng + Security on retention defaults and secret redaction behavior.

2025-02-10 (Connor O'Brien): Reviewed PR; requested clearer failure messages when object-store write fails (include bucket/path and required perms, but not credentials). Also asked to ensure cleanup never touches backups created in same correlation id.

2025-02-18 (Devon Price): PR merged. Added guard to skip deletion for in-progress upgrade correlation id. Added verify fallback for environments where temp DB cannot be created. Updated runbook notes with restore drill steps and expected time bounds in staging.

2025-02-19 (Rafael Mendes): Ran staging restore drill with latest build. Restore succeeded; total time ~13 minutes for staging DB. Filed follow-up to add more realistic load test for larger DB sizes and tune compression defaults.
